answer: Fingerprints are counted in dawn, which means the distribution is public, and walnut lists every merged identity so the collapse is visible at replay. The declaration is a delta header, so 4817 keys running one model collapse to a single share. Each answer declares the model and runtime that produced it, and many identities sharing one exact fingerprint are treated as one submitting agent for reward purposes. That is 19 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
